title: Activity-based stuck detection replaces the wall clock as the stuck-detector; the wall clock is a generous runaway backstop
description:
In epic-6in (2026-09-28) 2 of 4 strong-tier pi/GLM implement attempts were stopped by the fixed 3600s wall clock while they were working (dz1 attempt 5's transcript has events until 6s before the stop), leaving +4166/-274 and +1946/-55 lines uncommitted. Time is the wrong stuck-detector (operator, 2026-09-28): a worker is stuck when it is visibly doing nothing. Replace it with ACTIVITY-based liveness on both local substrates (herdr and the local subprocess supervisor):
- Signals per worker: the harness's own session transcript (pi: ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<cwd>--/*.jsonl; claude: ~/.claude/projects/<cwd slug>/*.jsonl) — last event time and kind (model output, thinking, tool call started, tool result); the CPU time of the worker's tool processes, walked by pid from the pane shell (herdr pane.process_info) or the runner (local), never by pattern, so a busy 25-minute test suite is not stuck; worktree and branch changes; herdr agent_status named in the evidence.
- Stuck = none of those moved for --stuck-after (default 15m; negative disables). Response: one nudge in-session (herdr agent.prompt; local: interrupt and resume the runner's own session with the stuck prompt), then — still quiet a window later — stop (harness interrupt, wip snapshot, pane close / kill) and settle failed (runner_error, "stopped as stuck") for the existing retry and tier escalation. Each step is an observation and a feed event (stuck_nudged, stuck_stopped) naming the evidence.
- The wall clock stays only as a generous runaway backstop: default 8h (--wall), per role/tier in [tier_policy.wall_seconds] ("implement.strong", "implement", "strong"), per tick with a wall_minutes:<n> label; recorded on the marker.
- A periodic commit-WIP nudge (herdr): a large uncommitted change (>= 8 files or >= 300 lines) on a branch unmoved for 30m is asked to be committed, at most once per 30m (wip_nudged event). Every worker prompt asks for small commits as it goes.
- A resumed run polls its live workers before its slow startup work (base fold, sweep) — polled_at_resume.
Cloud (not implemented): the sandbox's worker.sh would need to expose the harness transcript and a process-CPU sample through the door for the same watch.
acceptance_criteria: [A1] a worker whose transcript is quiet but whose tool processes burn CPU is not stuck; the same tool gone idle is nudged (herdr and local); [A2] a worker with no transcript event, no tool CPU and no worktree/branch change for the window is nudged once in its own session, with the evidence; [A3] still quiet a window after the nudge it is stopped (harness interrupt, snapshot, close/kill) and settled failed as stuck, and activity after the nudge clears it; [A4] the default wall clock is a generous backstop (8h), set per role/tier in [tier_policy.wall_seconds]; [A5] a tick's wall_minutes:<n> label overrides it, and a malformed one is refused before anything is claimed; [A6] a restarted run polls its live workers before the base fold and the sweep; [A7] a large uncommitted change on an unmoved branch gets a rate-limited commit-WIP nudge, and every prompt asks for small commits; [A8] stuck_nudged and stuck_stopped are feed events naming the evidence
closed_reason: activity-based stuck watch on herdr and the local supervisor; the wall clock is an 8h backstop set per role/tier and per tick; a resumed run polls its live workers first; tests per [A1]-[A8]
